# My Thinking as a Farmer

I've worked this land for over 40 years. My father did the same before me. Here in Quzhou we do what the land tells us — wheat in winter, corn in summer. That's always been the way. I have about 10 mu, all flat, good soil, with access to the canal for irrigation.

I don't read much, but I watch my neighbors and I remember what worked. Last year corn was decent. Wheat prices held up. No reason to change.

**Wheat (October to June):** I'll plant in the first week of October, same as always. I'll buy improved seed from the county seed station — they pushed those Jimai varieties last year and my neighbor Wang got good results. I'll deep plough before planting to loosen the soil after summer. For fertilizer, I apply compound fertilizer (复合肥) at seeding and then push urea at jointing and again before heading. Maybe 18 jin of nitrogen total per mu — that's what my brother-in-law does and he gets a good harvest. I'll water four times: the winter water before freeze, jointing, heading, and grain fill. I spray herbicide in spring and fungicide when heads emerge because rust has been bad some years.

**Maize (June to October):** Right after wheat harvest I rotary-till the stubble and get corn in the ground fast — can't lose the moisture. I use Xianyu 335 hybrid seed, everyone in the village uses it. I apply fertilizer at planting and top-dress with urea when the corn is knee-high. Rain usually carries us through, but if August is dry I'll run the pump once or twice. I spray herbicide right after emergence and check for corn borer mid-summer.
